title: I18n + Error Copy Quickstart for SDKs (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
A compact, pragmatic quickstart for shipping consistent, localized error copy across Redwood SDKs. Focus is on small friction wins (clear English copy baseline, stable error codes, translation flow, and telemetry hooks) so we can reduce developer confusion and surface operational problems faster.

Audience:
- SDK maintainers across JS/Python/Go
- Developer Experience writers/PMs
- Solutions engineers who onboard enterprise customers

Scope (what this doc covers):
- Lightweight schema for SDK error objects and codes
- Opinionated copy patterns in en-US (baseline) and guidance for translating to other locales
- Recommended file formats + loader pattern for each SDK (simple, testable)
- Telemetry/event hooks to track copy exposures and translation gaps
- Quick checklist for rollout and verification (manual + automated)

Non-goals:
- Full translation platform (we rely on vendor or partner for bulk translations)
- Deep localization of examples/docs beyond SDK surface errors

Problem we see today (notes from field):
- Inconsistent phrasing across SDKs: same backend error surfaces as different messages (confuses integrators).
- Missing stable codes: changing a human message breaks downstream logic.
- No signal for when untranslated messages reach users in target locales.
- Enterprise customers want precise, localized guidance for remediation (not generic 500s).

Principles (opinionated):
1) Stable machine-readable code is the contract (e.g., ERR_RATE_LIMIT). Never change codes in a minor release.
2) Human copy is mutable, tested, and lives outside code (translation files).
3) Default English copy should be short, action-oriented, and include a one-line remediation suggestion when helpful.
4) Telemetry should capture code exposure count + locale (so we can prioritize translations).
5) SDK should expose both raw error object and a helper that returns the localized message. Apps can opt-in to showing localized copy or the raw code.

Suggested SDK Error Schema (minimal):
- code: string (stable enum, e.g., ERR_INVALID_KEY, ERR_AUTH_EXPIRED, ERR_RATE_LIMIT)
- message: string (fallback English message)
- details: optional string (opaque, for logs)
- docs_url: optional string (link to remediation page)
Example JSON: {"code":"ERR_RATE_LIMIT","message":"Request rate limit exceeded. Try again after 60s.","docs_url":"https://docs.redwood.ai/errors#rate-limit"}

File format & placement (per SDK):
- JS/TS: /locales/{locale}.json (flat key map: ERR_RATE_LIMIT -> "..."), loader optional lazy require.
- Python: redwood_locales/{locale}.json (same shape), expose get_message(code, locale).
- Go: embed locale files in pkg/locales, provide Lookup(code, locale) with fallback to en-US.
Rationale: JSON is universally parsable and easy to patch. Keep files small (just error code -> string).

Canonical English copy templates (baseline):
- ERR_INVALID_KEY: "Invalid API key. Check your REDWOOD_API_KEY and try again."
- ERR_AUTH_EXPIRED: "Authentication expired. Reauthenticate or refresh your token."
- ERR_RATE_LIMIT: "Request rate limit exceeded. Retry after a short wait or contact support if it persists."
- ERR_NETWORK: "Network error — unable to reach Redwood. Check connectivity or set a longer timeout."
- ERR_MODEL_NOT_FOUND: "Requested model not available in this region. See docs for available models and regions."
Guidance: keep under 120 chars where possible; include next actionable step (what to try).

Translation workflow (fast path):
1) All new/updated English strings are added to /locales/en-US.json and a translation request ticket is opened (template in Confluence).
2) Use vendor (Crowdin/Transifex) or in-house PM to get target locales. Ask for short key context (one sentence).
3) Import translations as locale JSON files. Commit with change note referencing error codes changed.
4) SDK release: ship language files as patch. Avoid changing keys during translation window.

Telemetry & metrics (must-haves):
- sdk.error_shown (attrs: code, locale, sdk_name, version, route) — incremented whenever SDK surfaces a localized message to the calling app (we use exposure counts to prioritize).
- sdk.error_fallback (attrs: code, locale, sdk_name, version) — when locale had no translation and fallback occurred.
- sdk.error_unhandled (attrs: code, sdk_name, version) — when app did not catch and report error (helps SRE).
Dashboards: top 50 (code, locale) pairs with fallback rate > 5%.

Quickstart for SDK maintainers (30–60 min):
1) Add error schema to SDK's central error object. (5–10 min)
2) Add locales/en-US.json with the baseline English messages (10–15 min).
3) Wire a helper function getLocalizedMessage(code, locale) with fallback to en-US and emit sdk.error_shown and sdk.error_fallback events. (15–25 min)
4) Write two simple tests: one for English lookup, one that simulates a missing locale to assert fallback path and telemetry ping. (10–15 min)
5) Update CHANGELOG and mention stable codes contract. (2–5 min)

Testing & verification checklist (pre-release):
- Unit tests for all codes referenced in codebase.
- Smoke script to iterate locales and verify no missing keys for a given release subset.
- Manual spot check in target locale with sample flows (copy in UI where applicable).
- Verify telemetry events appear in staging (sdk.error_shown / sdk.error_fallback).

Rollout notes (enterprise):
- Feature flag: localized copy opt-in per-customer (some customers prefer raw codes for automation).
- Provide per-customer override mapping (customers can supply their own locale files for private deploys).
- For Private/VPC customers, include locale files in the package or provide a clear import path.

Sample copy templates for integration docs (short):
- Troubleshooting snippet for rate limit:
  "If you see ERR_RATE_LIMIT, consider batching requests, increasing backoff, or upgrading to Dedicated for predictable throughput. See docs: <docs_url>."

Open questions / TODOs (notes to self):
- How to best version translation files? (semver tie to SDK or separate translations version?)
- Should we include small pluralization patterns? (i.e., "1 request" vs "{n} requests") — for now lean no, until a string needs it.
- Decide on a single telemetry vendor event naming (prod/staging differences).
- Determine a lightweight CI step that fails a release if new error keys are missing translations for required locales (opt-in per release).

Example friction scenario (customer feedback):
- Customer sees "Internal server error" in Spanish — no remediation or link. They open support -> low-trust because message is vague. With this work, the message becomes "Error interno: fallo al procesar la petición. Reintente en 30s or contact support with code ERR_INTERNAL_500."

Notes for writers (explicit):
- Provide one-sentence context for each code when creating translation request. It reduces mistranslation.
- Prefer imperative verbs and clear named actions ("Reauthenticate", "Check API key").

References / links:
- Confluence guide (linked above) for templates used by translations team.
- GH PR template: redwood/sdk-localization#67 (use for automated import).
- Slack thread: #devex-localization (archived examples).

Immediate next steps (short):
- Maya: add en-US.json for JS SDK and wire getLocalizedMessage helper (due 2025-02-17).
- Jon: prototype telemetry pings for error exposures in staging (due 2025-02-21).
- Evelyn: align translation ticket template with PM (due 2025-02-24).

Unresolved/risks:
- If codes are not maintained strictly, translations will be inconsistent and we'll have to map old->new keys (painful).
- Adding pluralization/localization frameworks increases maintenance burden; keep it minimal unless required.

Appendix (snippets):
- Minimal JS helper example (pseudo):
  function getLocalizedMessage(code, locale) {
    const localeMap = loadLocale(locale) || loadLocale('en-US');
    const msg = localeMap[code] || localeMap['ERR_UNKNOWN'] || 'Unknown error';
    telemetry.emit('sdk.error_shown', {code, locale: locale || 'en-US'});
    if (!localeMap[code]) telemetry.emit('sdk.error_fallback', {code, locale});
    return msg;
  }

Notes to self: ship the en-US baseline first. Small wins — one clear message per code, telemetry for prioritization. Keep translations as a separate fast-follow sprint.

End of sketch.
